title: Hummus
subtitle: Classic Levantine chickpea dip
excerpt: Smooth, creamy hummus made from cooked chickpeas blended with tahini, lemon, and garlic. Homemade hummus is far better than shop-bought and comes together in a blender in minutes.

recipe.sourceNotes: Hummus bi tahini (chickpeas with tahini) is a staple across the Levant, with long roots in the cuisines of Lebanon, Syria, Palestine, Israel, Jordan, and Egypt. Written recipes appear in medieval Arab cookbooks.

recipeTools.notes: A high-powered blender or processor gives the smoothest result.

content.text: Hummus is a smooth paste of cooked chickpeas blended with tahini, lemon juice, and garlic. The texture should be very smooth, almost silky, not grainy. The best hummus is made from dried chickpeas cooked until completely soft, but very good hummus can be made from tinned chickpeas if you blend for long enough.
If using tinned chickpeas, warm them in their liquid in a small saucepan for 5 minutes. Drain, keeping about 4 tablespoons of the liquid.
Place the warm chickpeas in a food processor or blender. Add the tahini, lemon juice, garlic, and salt. Blend for 2 minutes.

With the machine running, add the ice-cold water one tablespoon at a time, and some of the reserved chickpea liquid if needed, blending for at least another 2 minutes until completely smooth. Taste for lemon and salt.
Spoon onto a plate, use the back of a spoon to spread it and create a shallow well. Drizzle over olive oil and dust with smoked paprika. Serve at room temperature.
